transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Basically, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaners, and... well, everything is just getting out of hand. The tickets, receipts, workshop notes, the customer jobs—they all just end up piled together in a mess. It gets to the point where I look at it and I honestly don't even know what to handle first.
Have you had this kind of trouble staying organized since you were a child?

Yes, I really have. Even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was a bright kid, but just... scattered. I was always talking out of turn in class, losing my assignments and papers, and they constantly had to give me reminders just to finish my work. So, yeah, it's been an issue for as long as I can remember.
As a child, were you often unable to sit still?

No, not really. I mean... I didn't have much of a problem staying in my seat. I was definitely distracted and, like I said, talking too much, but I wasn't really one of those kids bouncing off the walls or anything. So, no, sitting still wasn't really the issue for me.
Do you feel driven to repeatedly check or arrange things until they seem exactly right?

No, I don't really do that. If anything, it's the opposite. I mean, my stuff is just a mess, like I said. I don't really get stuck on making sure things are lined up perfectly or anything like that. I just... I just let it pile up until I don't know what to do with it.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about everyday things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

No, I wouldn't say I do. I mean, I have normal worries, you know, about paying bills or getting to work on time, but I don't sit around worrying about things for no reason. My mind is usually just jumping from one thing to the next too fast to really get stuck on worrying about one specific thing anyway.
